issues.t: Dual-clutch oil pump fault can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights and a fail-safe message, then after about 20–30 seconds the truck loses drive power, even at highway speed.
issues.why: The high-pressure electric oil pump inside the 8-speed wet dual-clutch transmission used with the turbo engine can develop an internal fault, and the fail-safe logic then lets the clutches disengage.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-746. The dealer inspects the transmission, replaces it if needed, and updates the software for free.

issues.t: Sudden limp mode, won't go faster than about 20 mph
issues.sym: The truck suddenly loses power and will not go faster than roughly 20 mph, often with warning lights. Restarting may or may not clear it.
issues.why: This is the powertrain's protective limp mode. Owners have reported it on both 2022 and 2023 trucks; on turbo models a transmission fault such as the oil pump problem covered by recall 22V-746 is a known trigger.
issues.next: Get safely off the road. Have the codes read by a Hyundai dealer and make sure every open recall and software update has been done.

issues.t: Dual-clutch judder and hesitation from a stop
issues.sym: A shudder, a flat spot or a delay when pulling away, jerky low-speed shifts, or a bump when the transmission engages.
issues.why: The 8-speed dual-clutch automatic relies on learned clutch engagement points. If that learning drifts, or the control software is out of date, takeoff feels rough. Hyundai issued a bulletin with software and relearn steps.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for transmission software updates and run the clutch relearn before any parts are replaced.

issues.t: Dual-clutch transmission noise at highway speed
issues.sym: A whine or droning noise from the transmission at speeds above about 40 mph.
issues.why: Owners have reported gear or bearing noise from the dual-clutch transmission. The cause has not been pinned to one part.
issues.next: Have a dealer road-test and record the noise while the truck is under warranty.

issues.t: Turbo oil supply pipe can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Oil smell or smoke from under the hood, or oil spots under the truck.
issues.why: On a very small batch of turbo trucks the oil feed pipe to the turbocharger could crack at its fitting and spray oil near hot parts, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-197. The dealer replaces the pipe for free.

issues.t: Tow hitch wiring module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. On trucks with a Hyundai-installed tow hitch, a fire can start near the rear even when parked.
issues.why: Water can get into the trailer wiring module behind the hitch and cause a short circuit.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall 23V-181. Park outside and away from buildings until the dealer installs a fuse and new wiring kit.

issues.t: Roof moldings may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or flapping from the roof, or a molding strip lifting or missing.
issues.why: The clips holding the roof moldings did not grip the roof flange well enough on early trucks, so a molding could come off while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-038. The dealer secures or replaces the moldings for free.

issues.t: Roof rail rattles or comes loose
issues.sym: Rattling, whistling or movement from the roof side rails.
issues.why: Owners have reported the roof rails working loose or not being secured well.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the rail fasteners, and confirm the roof molding recall has been done.

issues.t: Power steering assist can cut out (recall)
issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes heavy and a warning light comes on.
issues.why: A circuit board in the electric power steering unit was built with contaminated solder flux, which can short and shut off steering assist.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for recall 24V-412. The dealer replaces the steering power pack for free.

issues.t: Can shift out of Park without the brake (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter moves out of Park without your foot on the brake.
issues.why: Wiring in the center console was routed against the shift lock release, so the lock that holds the shifter in Park may not work.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-877. Always set the parking brake until the dealer reroutes the wiring.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may be installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No warning light or symptom.
issues.why: On a small number of trucks the side curtain airbags were not installed correctly at the factory and may not deploy properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-809. The dealer reinstalls the airbags for free.

issues.t: Unexpected automatic emergency braking (recall)
issues.sym: The truck brakes hard on its own with no obstacle ahead.
issues.why: Front camera software in the forward collision-avoidance system could misjudge the road ahead and trigger braking when it is not needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-316 and get the free camera software update.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The gauge screen goes dark and restarts while driving, so speed and warning lights disappear for a few seconds.
issues.why: A software error in the instrument cluster can make the display reboot.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for recall 26V-047. The update is free at the dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Tonneau cover won't latch or close flush
issues.sym: The bed cover won't lock or unlock, won't fully retract, or leaves a gap when closed.
issues.why: A broken or missing clip under the cover, or rail misalignment, keeps the latch from working. Hyundai issued a bulletin for diagnosing the cover.
issues.next: Clean the rails and have the dealer inspect the cover under warranty.

issues.t: Oil in the intake from a misassembled PCV valve
issues.sym: Blue-gray smoke on startup, oil in the air filter box or intake, or rising oil use.
issues.why: On some turbo engines the crankcase ventilation (PCV) check valve was put together wrong, letting engine oil get pulled into the intake and soak the air cleaner. Hyundai issued a bulletin to inspect and fix it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the PCV valve under bulletin 21-EM-012H, and keep an eye on the oil level until it is done.

issues.t: Check engine light for engine temperature control fault
issues.sym: A check engine or warning light with code P2181, sometimes with the temperature gauge acting oddly or weak cabin heat.
issues.why: These engines use an electronic thermal management module in place of a simple thermostat. Hyundai issued a bulletin for faults with this module setting code P2181.
issues.next: Have the code read. Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it reads hot. The dealer can test and replace the module under warranty.

issues.t: Steering wheel shake when braking
issues.sym: Vibration through the steering wheel or brake pedal when slowing from highway speed.
issues.why: Uneven front rotor wear or thickness variation causes brake judder. Hyundai published a bulletin on diagnosing and repairing it.
issues.next: Have the front rotors measured. Resurfacing or replacing the rotors and pads usually fixes it.

issues.t: Rough running or misfire from fuel injector faults
issues.sym: A check engine light, rough idle, misfire or hesitation.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a diagnostic bulletin for direct-injection fuel injectors on some 2022 trucks, since a leaking or sticking injector causes misfires.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer to follow the injector diagnostic bulletin. Injector replacement is a warranty item on these young trucks.

issues.t: Water leaks onto the front passenger floor from the windshield seal
issues.sym: Wet carpet or standing water on the front passenger side floor, usually after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: On some early 2024 trucks built from August to October 2023, the urethane seal between the windshield and the body has a gap near the passenger-side A-pillar. Hyundai issued a bulletin and service campaign (9A6) to fill it.
issues.next: Dry the carpet so it doesn't mildew or damage wiring, and ask a Hyundai dealer to check your VIN for the windshield seal campaign. The fix is quick and free when it applies.

issues.t: Check engine light for 8-speed transmission solenoid codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with harsh or odd shifting. A scan shows transmission solenoid or torque converter clutch codes (for example P0741, P0748 or P0753).
issues.why: On the non-turbo 2.5L with the regular 8-speed automatic, a faulty shift solenoid or the wiring harness inside the transmission can set these codes. Hyundai's bulletin 23-AT-003H tells dealers to replace the affected solenoid and the internal harness.
issues.next: Have the codes read soon and take it to a Hyundai dealer; the repair is covered by the powertrain warranty for original owners and by the bumper-to-bumper warranty for later owners while it lasts.
